plan_a_advantages: Dedicated tempo session for threshold development
Longer, controlled aerobic run to build endurance
Strength training component for injury prevention and stability
More balanced distribution of training types (aerobic, strength, easy runs)
plan_b_advantages: Hill repeats session for targeted strength
Recovery runs are important for preventing overtraining
Potentially more adaptable to individual recovery needs due to the emphasis on easy runs
Longer recovery runs could be beneficial for a runner who needs more time to recover
reasoning: Plan A is the better training plan for a trail runner aiming to become faster because it incorporates a more structured approach to building aerobic base and threshold strength. While Plan B includes hill work, it relies heavily on recovery runs, which, while important, don't directly contribute to speed development. Plan A’s inclusion of a dedicated tempo session and a longer, controlled aerobic run is crucial for increasing the runner’s lactate threshold and sustained effort capacity – key factors for faster trail running. Furthermore, the inclusion of strength training supports durability and injury prevention, which is vital for consistent progress.
